title: My story, so far
tagline: Review the old, discover the new.
intro: I’m a coder from Beijing and a parent of two. I’ve spent twenty years building software, and then data systems, at telecom companies, JD.com and Alibaba.

In my own time I build basketball models, lessons, apps and worlds you can play in. Each one starts from something old and makes something new. That’s the thread running through this story, and an old line from Confucius says it best.

motto.quote: Review the old to discover the new, and you can teach others.
motto.note: Every project in this story starts from something old and makes something new. Follow the thread.

blocks.text: I grew up in Beijing and studied economics at Henan University. But I’m very much a coder.
I really enjoy the process of generating something new with code.
That’s the thread through every chapter here: start from what already exists, and make something that didn’t exist before.

chapters.label: Languages
chapters.title: Five years in English, and now Japanese

blocks.text: From 2006 I built telecom software for China Mobile in Beijing and PCCW in Hong Kong, first as an engineer and then as a team lead. I spent five years on-site in Hong Kong, working in English every day.
Now I’m learning Japanese. I love Japan. To me, it is a democratic and civilised country.
Learning a language is the simplest case of reviewing the old to discover the new: old words, reviewed again and again, become new sentences. LesMots, an app I built, works the same way.

In 2012 I joined JD.com and led a team of 17 engineers building the software for Asia No.1, then Asia’s largest automated warehouse. On Double 11 in 2015 I led the on-site technical command while it shipped 502,000 orders in 24 hours with zero downtime, a single-warehouse world record at the time.

Since 2018 I’ve been at Alibaba: real-time data for Freshippo’s grocery stores, a shared data platform for four business units, and now the data behind Taobao Flash Sale, which handles more than ten million orders a day.
The work is reviewing the old to discover the new, every day. You read what already happened, carefully, and build what comes next on top of it.
I play basketball, and my son loves it a lot. I hope he can get the most advanced basketball training there is.
That’s why I sponsor Congdong Sports. And because I’m a coder, I also study the game the way I know best: with data.
Some things I build simply because I enjoy building them. The first three are private for now, so there’s no code to show yet.

chapters.label: Photos
chapters.title: The people and places in my story

blocks.text: And old towns: Suzhou’s canals and gardens, Chengdu’s lantern-lit lanes. The old, quite literally.
The line from Confucius ends with teaching: “…and you can teach others.”

I’ve led and mentored engineering teams of up to 17 people. I make the NBA Data Science Studio lessons so that anyone can learn statistics through questions about the game. And I keep reviewing the old to learn the new, every day.

ending.title: Thank you for reading
ending.text: I hope you understand me a little better now. If something here made you want to talk, write to me.
